title: He washed the feet that would walk away from Him.
paragraphs: He washed the feet that would walk away from Him.
Sit with that.

Not strangers.
Not enemies in the distance.
His own.

The hands that formed galaxies…
knelt in a dim room with a towel and a basin.

And in front of Him?
Dust.
Sweat.
Failure waiting to happen.
Gospel of John 13 doesn’t give us a polished moment. It gives us something uncomfortable. Raw. Holy.
Jesus knew.

He knew Peter would deny Him.
He knew Judas would betray Him.
He knew the rest would scatter like frightened sheep.
And still…
He washed.
Every.
Foot.

No hesitation.
No selective love.
No “I’ll serve you if you stay loyal.”
This is the kind of love heaven calls normal.
And here’s where it hits us—
We love with conditions.

“I’ll forgive… if they apologize.”
“I’ll serve… if they notice.”
“I’ll stay… if it’s easy.”
But Jesus?
“Just as I have loved you…” (John 13:34)

That’s not a suggestion.
That’s a standard.

And it’s impossible…
if we’re running on human strength.
Because human love gets tired.

Human love keeps receipts.
Human love remembers who hurt us and builds quiet walls.
But Jesus-love?

It moves toward the mess.
It kneels in front of failure.
It serves even when the story hasn’t changed yet.
Let that sink in.

He didn’t wait for Peter to become bold.
He didn’t wait for Judas to repent.
He didn’t wait for the disciples to prove they were worthy.
He loved them before they changed.
That’s the Gospel.
Book of Romans 5:8 says, “While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Not improved.
Not cleaned up.
Not spiritually impressive.
Sinners.

That means…
you don’t have to fix yourself to be loved by God.
But it also means something deeper—

If you’ve received that kind of love,
you are now called to reflect it.
And that’s where the tension lives.
Because loving like Jesus will cost you.

It will cost your pride.
It will cost your comfort.
It will cost your right to “get even.”
It may even cost your reputation.
But here’s what we miss—

Jesus didn’t just command this love.
He supplies it.
Through His Spirit.

You’re not being asked to manufacture something divine.
You’re being invited to surrender to it.
So when your heart says, “I can’t forgive them…”
Pause.
Remember the cross.
Remember the nails.
Remember the mercy that found you at your worst.
And then ask:
“Lord, love them through me… because I can’t do this on my own.”
That’s where transformation begins.

Not in trying harder—
but in surrendering deeper.
Some of you are holding onto bitterness right now.

You smile in public…
but inside, there’s a quiet coldness.
You’ve learned how to function without loving.
Jesus didn’t die for that version of you.
He died to make your heart alive again.

Soft again.
Bold again.
Capable of loving people who don’t deserve it.
Just like you didn’t.
Just like I didn’t.
This is not weak love.
This is war.

War against pride.
War against selfishness.
War against the lie that says, “Protect yourself at all costs.”
Jesus shows us a different way—

Lose your life…
and you’ll find it.

Give love…
even when it’s not returned.

Serve…
even when it’s not seen.

Forgive…
even when it’s not asked.
Why?
Because your reward is not in people’s response.
It’s in Christ.
And He sees.
Always.
So today, here’s the question:
Who’s the “dirty feet” in your life right now?

The one who hurt you.
The one who disappointed you.
The one who walked away.

Jesus is not asking you to ignore truth.
He’s not calling you to enable sin.
But He is calling you to love with His heart.

A love that is truthful…
but still tender.

A love that sets boundaries…
but never builds hatred.
A love that reflects the cross.
And maybe… just maybe…
Your obedience becomes the doorway for someone else’s redemption.
Because people don’t just hear the Gospel.
They feel it through how we love.

Let it confront you.
Let it heal you.
Let it change you.
Because that’s exactly where Jesus meets you.
